label: Evidence-backed IC memo for human review. Synthetic data, illustrative policies.

claims.text: Fleet maintenance scheduling software sold by subscription to around 1,400 fleet operators; headquartered in Amsterdam.
FY2025 revenue of EUR 88m, agreed to the audited accounts after the hardware restatement.

Recurring revenue is 71% (EUR 62.4m of EUR 88m) on the adviser's definition (base case); management's 80% (EUR 70.4m) also counts EUR 8m of implementation and training fees billed in subscription invoices.
Adjusted EBITDA bridge: EUR 26m (first IM) to EUR 24m after the hardware restatement to EUR 21.5m after the adviser excludes EUR 2.5m of unstarted office savings (base case).

Net revenue retention is 104% on recognised revenue excluding a one-off bundle sale to the largest customer (base case), below the 105% screening criterion; 111% including it, and management's 112% is on year-end ARR.
The top ten customers are 31% of revenue and the largest is 9%; gross logo churn was 6%.
One customer said switching away would take six to nine months because of telematics and parts-system integration; to test across more customers.
The market is fragmented: the top three vendors hold about 22% of an estimated EUR 3.1bn European market growing about 9% a year.
The largest customer can terminate on 90 days' notice after a change of ownership.
One expert heard in market conversations that the largest customer may re-tender in 2027; to verify through permitted diligence (customer call), not relied on.
There is no SOC 2 Type II report, which enterprise prospects have requested; a risk to plan for, not a blocker on its own.
Two contractors who wrote parts of the scheduling engine have not signed IP assignments.
About 38% of the codebase runs on an unsupported framework version; the adviser estimates 18 to 24 months and EUR 3m to EUR 4m to remediate, with no critical penetration-test findings.
Pricing headroom may be lower than planned: one customer indicated tolerance around 5% against a planned 6% list increase.
